chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ismail ibn Jabir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, Might and Majestic: 'And those in whose wealth is a known right, For the asker and the deprived.'

'Is it besides the Zakat?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the man whom Allah grants wealth from his possessions, so he gives from it a thousand, and two thousand, and three thousand, and the less and the more, so he connects with it his kin, and carries by it the burdens from his people.'
ai.seo_question: What does the 'known right' in wealth refer to besides Zakat?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the 'known right' (haqq ma'lum) in Surah Al-Ma'arij is interpreted as voluntary charity (sadaqah) distinct from obligatory Zakat, emphasizing the social responsibility of the wealthy. The Imam illustrates this by describing how a person endowed with abundance should distribute varying amounts to support kin and alleviate the burdens of the community, highlighting the practical application of wealth in fostering social solidarity.
